label: plan 17 r9 step 1 after
pinning: pinned to the 16 fastest of 28 logical processors (hybrid CPU; --no-pin to disable)

results.name: virtual/image grid walk Right, 600 cards
results.description: Press Right along a row of a grid of 600 image cards, a VirtualList whose item is a row of seven cards and the column the cursor is in there, as Aperture's library: the key makes the row again with its cards, their pictures, captions and badges

results.name: virtual/image grid walk Down, 600 cards
results.description: Press Down in the same grid, past the rows on screen and back: the key makes the row the cursor left and the row it reached, and the row scrolled in

results.name: virtual/image grid walk Right, 600 cards, cards handed back
results.description: The same walk with the rows keyed by their place and the cards by their films: a row made again hands back the cards the key did not change, and the patch puts them back untouched, so a key makes the two cards it moved between

results.name: virtual/image grid walk Down, 600 cards, cards handed back
results.description: The same walk Down: the two rows the cursor moved between keep all but the card it left and the card it reached; a row scrolled in is made whole

results.name: virtual/image grid across a change of columns, 600 cards, cards kept in their own row
results.description: Each step the window is 1440 wide (seven cards across) or 1300 (six) and the grid's columns follow, with its cards kept but handed back only into the row with their own row's key: rows are keyed by their first card's place, so only the first row's cards come back, and every other card on screen is made

results.name: virtual/image grid across a change of columns, 600 cards, cards kept
results.description: The same, with a card handed back into whatever row holds its place now while its own row is still in the list, as Aperture's library does: each card moves to its new row untouched

results.name: component/shelf walk Right, 5 shelves of 7 cards, every card made
results.description: A cursor walks along five shelves of seven poster cards in a scrolled page (Aperture's Home) and on from one shelf into the next; the page's Build makes every card of every shelf again on each move, as Aperture's Home did until plan 17's round 7

results.name: component/shelf walk Down, 5 shelves of 7 cards, every card made
results.description: The same page, the cursor moving down a column from shelf to shelf, the page scrolling to follow the focus

results.name: component/shelf walk Right, 5 shelves of 7 cards, cards kept
results.description: The same walk with the cards in a KeptElements: the page's Build hands back each card whose film and cursor are what it was made with, and makes the two the cursor moved between

results.name: component/shelf walk Down, 5 shelves of 7 cards, cards kept
results.description: The Down walk with the cards kept

results.name: component/shelf walk Right, 5 shelves of 7 cards, ring moved without a build
results.description: The same walk with no build: a move takes the ring off one live card and puts it on the next, which takes the keyboard (KeptElements.Live), as Aperture's Home does since plan 17's round 7

results.name: component/shelf walk Down, 5 shelves of 7 cards, ring moved without a build
results.description: The Down walk with no build, the page scrolling to follow the focus

results.name: a11y/image grid walk Down, 600 cards, keys 100 ms apart, bridge on
results.description: virtual/image grid walk Down at a reader's pace, a key every 100 ms, an accessibility client listening: each key makes rows of cards again, which changes the grid's children, and scrolls a row in now and then; the trees a key builds

results.name: a11y/image grid walk Down, 600 cards, keys 100 ms apart, UIA
results.description: The grid walk Down at a reader's pace with the UIA bridge: the trees a key builds, the wrapper upkeep and events of the rows made again

results.name: a11y/image grid walk Down, 600 cards, keys 100 ms apart, AT-SPI
results.description: The grid walk Down at a reader's pace with the AT-SPI bridge: the trees a key builds, the objects' upkeep and the signals of the rows made again
